_note: Projected per-tenant policy data: user_attributes / bucket_attributes / org_settings.freeze_writes, plus the s3_grants / group_grants grant superset the control plane projects. The gateway's rego reads these by name. This object is the 'data'. To push the policy module alongside it, wrap it as { "policy": "<rego source>", "data": { ... } }; a bare object (this file) uses the gateway's compiled-in default policy.
_v3_note: From grant_schema_version 3 (src/pdp/bundle.rs, ADR-009) the bundle also PLACES buckets: data.backend.id names the backend this bundle was projected for, and bucket_attributes is keyed by S3 name with exactly one owning tenant per bucket. A request for a bucket not listed here, listed under another tenant, or routed to a backend_id that does not match data.backend.id, is refused by the gateway itself, before the policy is asked; ListBuckets is answered straight from this index. object_name is the control plane's own name for the bucket (carried into audit records); created_at (RFC 3339) backs ListBuckets' reported creation date. Below version 3 none of this is read: grant_schema_version, data.backend and quota are all ignored by an older gateway or an unversioned bundle (the shape this file shipped before 0.4.0).
_quota_note: Byte quotas (ADR-010, src/quota.rs) are also v3-only and optional at every level: data.backend.quota, tenants.<t>.quota, and tenants.<t>.bucket_attributes.<bucket>.quota. Each is { limit_bytes, used_bytes, collected_at }; used_bytes is the control plane's last collection and the gateway counts what each replica has accepted since collected_at on top of it, refusing a write that would cross limit_bytes at any level with QuotaExceeded (403). Omit quota at a level to enforce nothing there (e.g. a backend with its own native per-bucket quota, such as Garage).

acme._s3_key_epoch_note: Revocation for long-lived derived per-principal keys (src/auth/derived.rs). `s3_key_epoch` is the lowest epoch such a key may carry and still be honoured; raising it revokes every outstanding key for the tenant at the next bundle poll. `s3_key_epochs` optionally raises the floor for ONE subject (keyed `sa:<client id>` / `user:<sub>`), so one compromised consumer can be cut off without touching the others; it can only ever tighten. ABSENCE OF `s3_key_epoch` DENIES every derived key for this tenant — so publishing it is the opt-in, and losing it fails closed.
